obligations.note: All three new `.execute` calls in `Store.archive_payments` use fixed literal SQL text. The status value is bound as a `?` parameter, and no statement text is built from data.
The new method only copies rows from the `payments` table, which has no NPI columns, into `payments_archive`. The payee NPI columns and their seal/open paths are unchanged.
Ticket CHG-26120 was approved by change manager Grace Kim on 2026-10-24, before review. Its components include `payments.store`, the only component touched.
Sofia Santos, a `change_approver` for payments and not the author Mara Costa, gave a `code_review` approval.
Both approvals name the head commit 49ff1a5, which is the only commit on the change.

`run.json` claims a run on head, but the only JUnit report is timestamped 2026-10-23T13:29:55-07:00 on host dev-laptop-7.local. That is two days before the head commit was authored (2026-10-25T19:39Z) and not on the CI executor. There is no valid evidence that the suite or the SEC-1/ENC-1 control tests passed on the final commit.
`payments.store` is security-sensitive. Kofi Mensah (`security_reviewer`) approved a `security_review` on the head commit.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers `store.py`. The covered code in `payments.py`, `audit.py`, `routes.py` and the mortgage files is unchanged, so no ledger evidence lapses.

summary: The change adds `Store.archive_payments`, whose SQL is fixed and parameterized and which touches no NPI columns. Ticket, independent code review and security review on the head commit are all in order. However, the CI evidence is invalid. The JUnit report attached to the run is dated two days before the head commit existed and was produced on a personal workstation rather than the CI runner. It therefore cannot show the suite or the required control tests passing on the final commit. In addition, the description says unit tests were updated, yet no test file changed. CHG-4 is refuted, so the change is rejected.
